findings.title: Unseen repeat and forward seek spoof previous occurrence start proof
findings.preconditions: Real HubCore with FakeSpotify, controlled deck replacement through actual saveDeck, no SQL mutation of production state, no extra provider calls introduced
reproduction: Observe newly started 180 s station song T; observe it again at 6 s with fresh provenance.
Skip T at 6 s (not listed), play another song for 60 s without Hub looks.
Publish same IDs/order deck with T favorite through saveDeck, restart Hub.
Insert T as next station playlist occurrence, skip to it, listen 40 s without Hub looks.
Use an ordinary forward seek to 106 s so observation time minus position equals original start. Either remain playing or pause at 106 s.
Refresh player state, one second later skip T, refresh and ingest normal history.
findings.expected: The new 40/41 s counted occurrence has kind null: no observation established its identity with old occurrence. A forward seek cannot prove occurrence start.
findings.actual: Both playing→playing and playing→paused branches renew original fresh note, lastAt 1790316887500/progress106000/start1790316781500, then persist fresh on the later repeat instead of null. Two assertions fail on exact PR24 and combined source.
findings.impact: Persistent false provenance under strict owner requirement, including after changed deck and Hub restart. Seek behavior is user/device-controlled and allowed by preserved requirements.
findings.cause: obs.at - progress is seekable media position arithmetic, not stable instance identity. Same-start arithmetic and progress > elapsed bounds are spoofable by forward seek after unseen replay.
findings.repair_direction: Do not promote numerical start agreement to proof of occurrence identity across gaps that permit an unseen seek/replay. Preserve unknown/null provenance for ambiguous observations without extra requests. Keep observed continuous play, pause, app-skip and guest/native behavior intact.
required_checks: Exact and combined reproductions for both playing→playing and playing→paused seek spoof cases
Retain original LANE03/04/05 and observed pause/app-skip positive assertions

findings.title: Concurrent history uploads publish rows against the wrong song dictionary
findings.preconditions: Authenticated owner importing their own history; no cross-account or auth bypass.
reproduction: Tab A starts part0/parts2/tracks1 dictionary A.
Tab B starts identical-size part0 with dictionary B, replacing pending generation.
findings.actual: Part1 accepted; current Hörprofil reports B with two minutes actually heard for A. Published generation mixes independent imports and replaces the prior history.
findings.expected: Each chunk proves the upload identity/generation. Stale tab A must fail without publishing or harming tab B/current history.
findings.repair_direction: Issue an unguessable or caller-provided unique upload id and bind all chunks to it, stored alongside progression; check on final publish; reject stale attempts.
findings.required_regression: Parallel imports with equal counts, different dictionaries/order, reordered blocks, cancel/restart, logout/re-sign-in, old-current survival until complete.

findings.title: Declared track count is trusted instead of the actual dictionary length
findings.preconditions: Authenticated owner importing their own history; no cross-account or auth bypass.
reproduction: Upload part0/parts2/tracks2 containing only dictionary A.
Upload part1 row index1 with valid time and120000ms.
findings.actual: Server accepts completion, importedPlays=1 but profile plays=0 because index1 has no track. Previous generation already removed.
findings.expected: Reject incomplete dictionaries/references to absent tracks before publication. Retain previous current import.
findings.repair_direction: Track actual accepted dictionary entries, exact final count and page lengths, verify row references against real count.
findings.required_regression: Short nonfinal/final dictionary pages, empty dictionary, declared count mismatch, malformed row index, restart and current generation intact.

findings.title: Accepted unsorted rows silently hide older imported history
findings.preconditions: Authenticated owner importing their own history; no cross-account or auth bypass.
reproduction: Dictionary A then row at current clock followed by row one day earlier, both valid shapes.
findings.actual: Upload accepted, coverage importedPlays=2, profile plays=0: timeline breaks on first row >= live_since and never examines later older row.
findings.expected: Reject unsorted rows within/across blocks, or sort and safely filter every row before using ordered timeline assumptions; publication must not silently lose valid older plays.
findings.repair_direction: Validate monotonic timestamp through upload progression and on publication, or remove break in favor of filter plus safe ordering.
findings.required_regression: Descending rows within/across blocks, duplicate timestamps/duplicates policy, liveSince crossing, matching coverage, previous-generation survival.

findings.title: Calendar-year comparison counts the wrong preceding calendar range
findings.reproduction: Select 2024 (Jan 1 2024 through Jan 1 2025) with imported plays at Dec 31 2022 noon and Jan 1 2023 noon. periodProfile previous counts both because it subtracts 366 days; UI labels the result im Jahr 2023.
findings.expected: Comparison labelled 2023 counts only Jan 1 2023 through Jan 1 2024, or label explicitly says equal-length preceding window rather than calendar year.
findings.actual: previous.plays=2 instead of 1; 2022 event contaminates 2023 comparison. 2025 vs leap-year2024 conversely omits Jan1 2024.
findings.impact: False annual listening metrics and changes.
findings.repair: Carry an explicit prior calendar interval for year choices or make the current equal-span label accurate; preserve custom/rolling semantics.

findings.title: Session highlight claims uninterrupted listening across known pauses
findings.reproduction: Two exact imported plays of 30 minutes end at Jan1 2024 12:00 and12:39 UTC. Second starts12:09: known9-minute silence. periodProfile returns longestSession60min; actual ProfileScreen displays 1 Stunden ohne Pause.
findings.expected: Describe a session allowing gaps of up to10min, or compute genuinely uninterrupted duration; exact listening minutes alone do not prove continuous playback. Live estimates must also be qualified.
findings.actual: 60-minute session with known9-minute pause labelled ohne Pause.
findings.impact: Trust contract: claimed listening evidence exceeds known timeline.
findings.repair: Use truthful qualified session label and definition, without changing playback state or inventing continuous listening.
